segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So be imitators of God, as dearly loved children,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and walk in love, just as Christ also loved us and gave himself up for us, an offering and sacrifice to God, a fragrant aroma.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But sexual immorality and impurity of any kind, or greed, must not even be named among you, as is fitting for holy ones,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: nor obscenity, nor foolish talk or crude joking, which are out of place, but rather thanksgiving.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For of this you can be sure: no sexually immoral or impure or greedy person—that is, an idolater—has any inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Let no one deceive you with empty words, for because of these things the wrath of God is coming on the sons of disobedience.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So do not be partners with them;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. Walk as children of light,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for the fruit of the light is found in all goodness and righteousness and truth,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and discern what is pleasing to the Lord.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Take no part in the fruitless works of darkness, but rather expose them,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for it is shameful even to speak of the things done by them in secret.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But everything that is exposed by the light becomes visible,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for everything that becomes visible is light. Therefore it says:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “Wake up, sleeper, and rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So look carefully at how you walk, not as unwise people but as wise,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: making the most of the time, because the days are evil.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For this reason do not be foolish, but understand what the will of the Lord is.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And do not get drunk on wine, in which there is debauchery, but be filled by the Spirit,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: speaking to one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making music with your heart to the Lord,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: giving thanks always for everything, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to God the Father,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: submitting to one another out of reverence for Christ.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Wives, submit to your own husbands as to the Lord,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for a husband is head of his wife as Christ also is head of the assembly, he himself being the savior of the body.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But as the assembly submits to Christ, so also wives should submit to their husbands in everything.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the assembly and gave himself up for her,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: so that he might make her holy, cleansing her by the washing of water with the word,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: so that he himself might present the assembly to himself in glory, having no stain or wrinkle or anything of the sort, but so that she might be holy and without blemish.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In the same way husbands too ought to love their own wives as their own bodies. The one who loves his own wife loves himself,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for no one ever hated his own flesh; rather, he nourishes and cherishes it, just as Christ also does the assembly,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: because we are members of his body.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: This mystery is great, but I am speaking of Christ and the assembly.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In any case, each one of you as well must love his own wife as himself, and the wife is to show reverence for her husband.

notes.note: The traditional rendering is 'saints', which many translations keep; others use 'God's people'. The word is used of all members of the community as people set apart for God, echoing the Septuagint's language for Israel. 'Saints' now suggests canonised individuals or people of unusual virtue, which is not the meaning here.

The formula is the one used to introduce Scripture in 4:8, but the lines that follow do not match any known Old Testament passage, though they echo Isaiah 26:19 and 60:1. Most scholars think they come from an early Christian hymn, perhaps one sung at baptism. The source is not certain.

notes.phrase: making the most of the time
notes.note: The verb is a marketplace word meaning to buy up or buy back, and the noun for 'time' means a season or opportunity, not clock time. Most scholars take the phrase to mean seizing every opportunity while it lasts. The older rendering 'redeeming the time' keeps the commercial image but is now hard to understand.

The Greek preposition here normally marks means or sphere rather than content, so 'by the Spirit' is the more natural reading: the Spirit is the one who fills. Most English versions have 'with the Spirit', making the Spirit what one is filled with, and that reading remains possible. A minority read 'in spirit', referring to the human spirit.

The Greek word is the ordinary one for 'fear', which also covers the awe and respect owed to someone of higher standing. The related verb is rendered 'show reverence for' in verse 33, so that the reader can see the section opens and closes with the same idea. Some translations keep 'fear' in both places; 'respect' is the common choice in verse 33.

The earliest manuscripts, including Papyrus 46 and Codex Vaticanus, have no verb in this verse; it reads 'wives, to your own husbands as to the Lord', borrowing its verb from 'submitting to one another' in verse 21. Many other manuscripts supply the verb. English needs one, so it is supplied here, but the instruction to wives grammatically depends on the mutual submission of verse 21.

The traditional rendering is 'church', which is near-universal. A first-century hearer knew the word as a civic gathering and as the Septuagint's term for Israel assembled before God. 'Church' now suggests a building or an institution. 'Assembly' is used throughout this translation so the reader can see it is one Greek word.

The metaphorical force of 'head' is disputed. Most lexicographers take it to mean one who holds authority or pre-eminence, a use found in the Septuagint for leaders; some scholars argue for 'source', as of a river. The literal word is kept because the passage plays on head and body.

notes.phrase: by the washing of water with the word
notes.traditional: with the washing of water by the word
notes.note: The 'washing' is commonly taken as baptism, perhaps with the image of a bride's bath before her wedding in view. 'The word' is a term for something spoken; it may mean the proclaimed gospel, a confession made at baptism, or words spoken over the person baptised. The Greek does not settle which.

notes.traditional: members of his body, of his flesh, and of his bones
notes.note: Many later manuscripts add 'of his flesh and of his bones', echoing Genesis 2:23, and the King James Version includes the words. The earliest witnesses lack them, and most editors judge them a later expansion, though some argue they were dropped by accident.

In Paul's usage the word means a secret in God's purposes, once hidden and now disclosed, not a puzzle or something beyond understanding. Here the secret is that the 'one flesh' union of Genesis 2:24 points to Christ and the assembly. The Latin Vulgate rendered the word sacramentum, which shaped the later view of marriage as a sacrament.

candidates.reason: Recurs across Paul, the Gospels and Revelation; 'mystery' suggests a puzzle where the Greek means a disclosed secret, so translators could split between 'mystery' and 'secret'.
Frequent across the New Testament and variously rendered 'fornication', 'sexual immorality' or 'prostitution'; one decision on its range is needed.
The figurative use for conduct is pervasive in Paul and John; chapters will differ between 'walk' and 'live' unless a rule is set.
Used for wives, slaves, citizens, the assembly and Christ himself; 'submit', 'be subject' and 'be subordinate' carry different tones and should not vary by chapter.
The fear/reverence/respect choice for φόβος and φοβέομαι toward God, Christ and human superiors recurs in many books and affects how readers hear the texts.
